title: A Positive Test
statement: A disease affects $1\%$ of people. A test detects it $99\%$ of the time when present, and gives a false positive $5\%$ of the time when absent. You test positive. What is the probability you have the disease?
insight: Imagine 10,000 people: 99 true positives versus 495 false positives.
redHerring: Answering 99% by confusing P(positive | sick) with P(sick | positive).
hints: Picture a concrete crowd of 10,000 people.
How many are sick and test positive? How many are healthy and test positive?
Your answer is the share of all positives that are sick.
solution:
Out of 10,000 people, 100 are sick and 99 of those test positive. Of the 9,900 healthy people, $5\%$, or 495, test positive.

$P(\text{sick}\mid+) = \tfrac{99}{99+495} = \tfrac{99}{594} = \tfrac16$.
